old_problem: Earlier reviews could not tell whether Scalable visualization meant Mosaic/SVS, vGPU, multi-GPU spanning or another project feature because Procedure and Criteria were TBD. DeepSeek's generic state/readback concept omitted the actual NVIDIA Display Mode Selector firmware path and could not prove physical output or BAR1. Treating the label as an arbitrary multi-device solution would either invent coverage or issue a high-risk board update without a defined target.
disposition_reason: Resolve Engineering Decision Pending and BLOCKED. NVIDIA's authoritative Display Mode Selector guide names `physical_display_enabled_8GB_bar1` specifically for scalable-visualization use cases such as broadcast, virtual production and location-based entertainment. Together with the adjacent independent Display off(default) and Display enabled Items, this is sufficient to establish the intended vendor mode without guessing Mosaic, vGPU or application-level synchronization. The same guide defines supported boards, compatible driver families, exact single-adapter syntax, firmware risk and reboot activation. Exact GPU/OEM qualification, physical display path, pinned tool/driver, application smoke/visual oracle, final-state restoration and recovery are project/runtime bindings. The record preserves real visual evidence under ED-08/ED-20 and does not claim a mode readback alone proves an entire scalable solution.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1778, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 blocked record, original pending/blocked analyses, exact-code search, adjacent rows 1777/1779 and ED rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1779 / Wistron-HW-00412-V002 / 4903280be55a467e.

NVIDIA defines Physical Display Ports Enabled with 8GB BAR1 as the mode for scalable-visualization use cases including broadcast, virtual production and location-based entertainment. This exact wording is a stronger source than DeepSeek's generic GPU/vGPU interpretation.

The defined target is `physical_display_enabled_8GB_bar1`, distinct from `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1` in the separate Display enabled case and `physical_display_disabled` in the separate default-off case. Source identities and evidence are not merged.

NVIDIA's compatibility table supports physical-display-enabled modes with RTX Enterprise and Data Center drivers but not the vGPU driver. Driver family, board model, VBIOS and OEM qualification are therefore mandatory gates; vGPU deployment cannot be silently reused.

The Display Mode Selector writes board firmware, requires administrator privilege and reboot, and can affect all eligible boards when index is omitted. Only one serial/UUID/BDF-to-index-bound target may be updated after immediate approval and stable-power/workload drain.

Post-reboot BAR1 total and active mode plus actual physical-output evidence are both necessary. A blank/working screen alone cannot prove 8GB BAR1, and `nvidia-smi`/NVML Display Active alone only reports monitor connection rather than the board firmware configuration.

The row validates the scalable-visualization display mode, not a complete Mosaic/frame-lock/multi-GPU application. An owner-approved representative physical-output workload confirms usable graphics output without inventing topology coverage absent from this Source Key.
No Display Mode Selector command, firmware update, reboot, physical display action, log clear or other DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: NVIDIA Scalable Visualization Mode — physical display enabled with 8GB BAR1
test_case.purpose: On one exact supported and OEM-qualified NVIDIA GPU, transition to `physical_display_enabled_8GB_bar1`, activate it through the required reboot, prove the active 8GB BAR1/physical-display state and usable visual output with an approved representative workload, then leave or restore the signed final mode without affecting other adapters.
required_package: Exact SUT and supported GPU model/SKU/serial/UUID/PCI BDF plus verified Display Mode Selector adapter index, VBIOS and pre-state mode/BAR1
OEM/vGPU-certified system approval for 8GB-BAR1 scalable mode and proof the hardware/firmware address-space configuration supports it
NVIDIA-authorized hash/version-pinned Display Mode Selector and a compatible RTX Enterprise or Data Center driver; no unsupported vGPU-driver substitution
Exact physical connector/cable/display/EDID/resolution path and owner-approved representative broadcast/virtual-production/location-based-entertainment output workload with visual acceptance

Dedicated maintenance, workload/display drain, stable power, immediate firmware/reboot approval, independent BMC/SSH/non-target display recovery, signed original/final-mode restoration artifact and vendor/OEM service path
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED; destructive firmware/reboot approval required. Bind the target serial/UUID/BDF to one tool index, verify board/VBIOS/OEM/driver support, preserve current mode, BAR1, PCIe/GPU/driver/workload/display/EDID and OS/BMC events, and prove recovery/stable power. Drain graphics/compute/vGPU users, obtain immediate confirmation and invoke the pinned tool once for only that adapter: `displaymodeselector --gpumode physical_display_enabled_8GB_bar1 -i <VERIFIED_INDEX>`. Capture full output, perform the required approved reboot, then verify active target mode, approximately vendor-defined 8GB BAR1 capacity, same GPU identity/PCIe health and compatible driver. A qualified operator or validated capture path runs the approved representative physical-output workload and records real visual output/EDID/resolution evidence. Restore the signed final mode only through a separately approved one-time vendor transition and required reboot. Never omit `-i`, use a vGPU driver, treat mode/readback as visual proof, clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Exactly the selected supported GPU changes to and activates `physical_display_enabled_8GB_bar1` after one approved write/reboot; all other adapters retain their pre-state. The target exposes the vendor-defined 8GB BAR1 and enabled physical ports with the compatible driver, produces stable correct output on the approved display/workload path, and retains healthy VBIOS identity, PCIe link, GPU/driver status, host services and preserved events. The signed final mode is reached and no recovery is needed or any owner-directed recovery is fully documented.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authoritative board/OEM/driver applicability, one-target firmware transcript, post-reboot active 8GB-BAR1 mode, unchanged non-target adapters, actual timestamped physical visual evidence, healthy GPU/PCIe/driver/host state and final-mode proof. Mode-selector success alone, nvidia-smi Display Active, BAR1 alone, a generic GUI screenshot or unverified application does not PASS. Unsupported hardware is N/A only with authoritative applicability evidence; missing package/qualification/recovery is BLOCKED. Wrong/all-GPU update, BAR1/mode mismatch, no/corrupt/unstable output, driver incompatibility, GPU loss, event regression or failed restore is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Require exact supported model/VBIOS, OEM-qualified platform, compatible non-vGPU driver and pinned vendor package; do not generalize 8GB-BAR1 mode to an unlisted board or uncertified host.
Map serial/UUID/BDF to tool index immediately before action and always supply `-i <VERIFIED_INDEX>`; omission can update every switchable adapter.

Treat each transition/restore as a separate GPU firmware write plus reboot requiring stable power, drained sessions/workloads, independent management/display path, immediate approval and one attempt only.
Require both machine mode/BAR1 evidence and genuine physical-output evidence; do not substitute remote request success or monitor-connected telemetry for pixels and usable workload output.
Stop on compatibility, write, reboot, PCIe, GPU, driver, BAR1, output or evidence anomaly. Do not retry, switch another mode, reboot or power-cycle automatically.
expected_evidence: Source Key/Variant, mode-specific owner approval, supported model/OEM/driver references, SUT/GPU serial/UUID/BDF/index and tool/VBIOS/driver hashes/versions
Pre-state mode/BAR1, PCIe/GPU/driver/workload/display/EDID identity, preserved OS/BMC/GPU events, stable-power/maintenance/reboot approval and recovery readiness
Exact scoped 8GB-BAR1 selector command with full stdout/stderr/exit status and no-retry/no-other-adapter audit
Required reboot/OS-ready timeline, active mode, BAR1, same-GPU/PCIe/driver health and real timestamped display/workload visual evidence with EDID/resolution
Final-state or separately approved restore transcript/reboot, complete health/events, recovery actions and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/N/A verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity, unsupported combination, selector error, incomplete firmware update, reboot failure, missing GPU, BAR1/mode mismatch, driver fault or lost/corrupt output, stop and preserve tool, mode/VBIOS, console and event evidence. Do not rerun or choose another mode. Use independent BMC/SSH/non-target display and the owner/OEM-approved signed prior-mode recovery or board-service procedure; any restoration is a separately approved scoped firmware transition with its own reboot and evidence.
